name: Photoluminescence of single NV centres versus axial magnetic field up to 5 T at 4 K in a closed-cycle vector-magnet confocal cryostat
plain_name: Watch how single diamond defects glow in a strong magnetic field at 4 K
description: Address individual NV centres (bulk ones under solid immersion lenses and shallow ones in nanopillars) with a 532 nm confocal microscope in a closed-cycle refrigerator at about 4 K, align the field along the NV axis with a (1,1,5) T vector magnet and record photoluminescence and ODMR contrast for fields up to 5 T to locate excited-state level anticrossings.
keywords: Watch how single diamond defects glow in a strong magnetic field at 4 K

sources.citation: Low-Temperature Photophysics of Single Nitrogen-Vacancy Centers in Diamond (Happacher et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 128, 177401, 2022)
Low temperature photo-physics of single NV centers in diamond (Happacher et al., arXiv:2105.08075, supplementary material)

reported_equipment: confocal microscope with a green excitation laser at 532 nm (Coherent Compass 315M)

requirements.rationale: All data were recorded with samples held at about 4 K.
Confocal excitation at 532 nm and PL collection need free-space optical access to the sample.
PL versus field was examined up to B_NV = 5 T.
The field must be aligned along the NV axis, which requires three-axis vector field control.
Optional: ODMR/spin-contrast measurements deliver microwaves through a 25 um Al wire next to the NV; pure PL-versus-field scans do not need it.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
